resolutions.recommendation: keep row; note Romanian side is back in the 2026-2035 Transgaz plan; check status and cost with the Ukrainian operator
resolutions.researcher_notes: The project is real. ENTSOG's 2020 plan lists it as TRA-N-502, a 30 km, 700 mm pipe near Khotyn, tied to the Romanian project TRA-N-596 under one EU project code. Length, diameter, location and pre-final-investment-decision stage all match the sheet. Capacity is given only in energy units. The 40 million euro cost has no source. The Transgaz plan for 2026 to 2035 (shareholders approved July 2026) lists the Romanian Gheraesti to Siret link again, 130 km, 450 million euros, target 2032. No Ukrainian document confirms the Ukrainian part is cancelled or revived. Not a duplicate of any other roster row.

resolutions.recommendation: split ownership by section; Gazprom PJSC at 100 percent fits only the Russian stretch; find the Ukrainian section owner and operator
resolutions.researcher_notes: The line is real. A Kursk encyclopedia entry, Ukrainian Wikipedia and a 2022 Interfax report on Gazprom's rebuild of a 40 km stretch all name it. It is a transmission trunk, so classification is fine. The row crosses from Ukraine to Russia, but Gazprom owns only the Russian side. Ukrainian Wikipedia says the two sections now work separately. No source was found that names the Ukrainian owner or operator. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 1 surviving ref(s) from 1 publisher(s) -> no.

resolutions.recommendation: change StartYear1 from 1960 to 1959; record diameters as 700, 800, 1020 mm or add a note; capacity of 13 is unsupported
resolutions.researcher_notes: Start year: a Kursk encyclopedia entry and a second Russian source put the end of construction and start of operation in 1959. resolutions.recommendation: no duplicate; it shares the Shebelinka start only with P3381 and P3382, which end at Slovyansk

resolutions.recommendation: Check whether capacity 200 million cubic meters per day and diameter 1400 mm describe one pipe or the whole multi-line Uzhhorod to Veľké Kapušany crossing. Also check P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod), whose end section may be the same pipe, and P0780.
resolutions.researcher_notes: The crossing is real: Eustream lists Veľké Kapušany as the entry and exit point to Ukraine, and the Ukraine to Slovakia flow was halted on 1 January 2025. But Eustream describes four to five parallel pipes of mostly 48 and 56 inch at that point and a station entry flow of 220 million cubic meters per day. The sheet shows one pipe of 14.5 km, 1400 mm and 200 million cubic meters per day (7062.93 MMcf/d), which looks like a crossing total or a mixed value. No source found names this segment or its length. Possible overlap with the end of P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod), not settled on documents.

resolutions.recommendation: treat P3381 and P3382 as one pipeline in two stages of rebuild; merge or re-scope so the DN 700 and DN 500 stretches do not both claim the same corridor
resolutions.researcher_notes: The pipeline is real. So P3381 (700 mm, 70 km) and P3382 (500 mm, 54 km) very likely describe the same physical corridor before and after rebuild. No source describes two parallel lines. The sheet's two rows share one route file that does not follow the named corridor, so it cannot help decide. Not touching lengths until a person rules on the merge. Wikipedia and the operator notices both give 67 km for the rebuild span.

resolutions.recommendation: merge into P3381 or re-scope as the rebuilt DN 500 stretches of the same line; keep one row per physical corridor
resolutions.researcher_notes: This row has the same name as P3381 and no source describes a second line. This row (500 mm, 54 km, built 2020) most likely records the rebuilt sections of the same corridor that P3381 records as the old 700 mm pipe. resolutions.recommendation: Rule whether P5989 should be narrowed to the new Berdyansk to Melitopol part or merged with P7817, P7818 and P1457.
